research_goal: Implement a small manager-as-tools orchestration planning CLI for the existing agent-platform project.
coding_context: agent-platform Python CLI, agent specs under configs/agents, and framework-neutral agent orchestration registry.
source_value_provenance: manager-as-tools pattern and handoff trade-off <- OpenAI Agents SDK orchestration docs checked on 2026-06-04
subagents/router/handoff/custom workflow pattern list <- LangChain multi-agent docs checked on 2026-06-04
Flow manages state/control and Crew handles agent collaboration <- CrewAI introduction checked on 2026-06-04
existing CLI and registry loading patterns <- agent-platform/src/agent_platform/cli.py and core registry source
plan_evidence: Use a deterministic planner first <- existing review noted runtime orchestrator was missing, but installing a framework requires separate audit
Keep Python implementation <- agent-platform README and existing CLI modules are Python-first
Expose subagents as generated tool records <- OpenAI agents-as-tools example and LangChain subagents pattern
Validate with unit tests and CLI checks <- existing agent_orchestration.py test style
stack_version_constraints: No external runtime framework dependency is installed in this change.
issue_discussion_notes: Checked issue/discussion surfaces as risk and adoption signals for manager/supervisor patterns; they do not override official docs or local validation.
Open-source issue counts and discussions indicate these patterns need observability and bounded handoff contracts, which the local planner records explicitly.
community_signal_notes: GitHub stars, issue counts, and discussions were treated as adoption and discovery signals only; implementation decisions use official docs and local repository contracts.
language_options: Python 3.11 for deterministic local CLI, dataclass parsing, unit tests, and existing platform code.
TypeScript for a future UI-facing orchestration editor or OpenAI Agents JS adapter.
language_decision_notes: Selected Python because agent-platform already uses Python modules, unittest, argparse, and JSON configs.
Rejected TypeScript for this change because no UI/runtime adapter is being implemented and a Python CLI is faster to validate against existing tests.
code_reference_notes: Existing CLI handlers parse JSON inputs, call pure functions, and print JSON reports; the new command follows that pattern.
Existing orchestration checker returns status, requires_rework, checks, gaps, warnings, and follow_up_actions; the planner follows the same report style.
OpenAI example shows a manager exposing specialist agents as tools, so the local planner emits tool_name and tool_description records for each subagent.
architecture_options: Framework-neutral deterministic planner that emits manager/subagent tool plans without running a model.
Install and integrate an external runtime framework such as OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or CrewAI immediately.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected framework-neutral deterministic planner because it fills the existing tool gap while preserving the repository's adapter-neutral boundary.
Rejected immediate runtime framework integration because installation audit, provider configuration, runtime resource guard, and adapter design are separate larger tasks.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Official docs support both code-driven and LLM-driven orchestration; this implementation chooses code-driven planning for deterministic validation.
Practitioner/reference implementations show real manager tool execution, but local readiness first needs a stable agent roster and tool access contract.
folder_structure_options: Add planner under agent_platform/orchestration beside the registry checker.
Create a new agent_platform/tools package for orchestration planning tools.
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected agent_platform/orchestration because the planner consumes the orchestration registry and belongs to the same capability boundary.
Rejected a new tools package because this is not a generic utility; it is an orchestration contract helper.
folder_semantics_notes: agent_platform/orchestration contains reusable agent creation and orchestration contract logic.
configs/orchestration contains registry and plan input templates.
tests/test_manager_tool_orchestration.py covers deterministic manager/subagent planning behavior.
maintainability_notes: The pure-function planner is easy to unit test and does not require network calls, provider credentials, or process lifecycle cleanup.
The generated plan remains framework-neutral, so future runtime adapters can consume it without changing requirements or agent specs.
findings: OpenAI and LangChain both describe manager/subagent-as-tool patterns where the manager keeps routing and final response control.
CrewAI separates stateful process flow from agent teams, reinforcing the need for explicit state/control planning before runtime execution.
The local repository already has agent specs and orchestration pattern contracts, so a deterministic planner is the smallest missing implementation asset.
options: Implement deterministic planner now and defer runtime adapter.
Install a full multi-agent framework now.
Only update documentation and leave runtime/tool gap open.
recommendation: Implement deterministic Python manager-as-tools planner and CLI, then validate with unit tests and existing config/orchestration checks.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Verified official manager/subagent/tool patterns, existing repository CLI shape, and the prior gap that no runtime/planner existed.
post_research_answers.best_option: Add a deterministic Python planner that emits manager/subagent tool plans.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It is the smallest implementation that satisfies the user's structure request without prematurely installing a runtime framework.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: Prompt-only documentation was rejected because it is not a tool; immediate framework installation was rejected because it needs a separate installation and adapter audit.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Add manager_tool.py, CLI command, template config, tests, agent spec/tool docs, requirements/spec/history/evaluation records.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: The planner does not execute subagents yet; future runtime adapters need resource, observability, installation, and provider configuration work.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Run unit tests, plan-agent-orchestration, check-agent-orchestration, inspect-agent, check-config-contract, omission, grounding, and evaluate-work.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: Capture manager-as-tools planner rules in agent-platform docs and history so future runtime adapter work can consume the plan contract.

risks_or_unknowns: No actual LLM execution is included.
Auto-selection uses deterministic keyword matching and may need a smarter scorer after real usage.
Future runtime execution must add resource lifecycle and trace storage checks.
